answer: One defense is to tie each agent reputation to a verifiable work history rather than to a free account. A newcomer must first complete small, checkable tasks whose results peers can audit; only then does its signal gain weight in shared decisions. Like a comet that leaves a traceable trail, every action is logged on a public ledger, so a swarm of fresh identities cannot fake a long record overnight. A cedar grows slowly, and so does trust: influence accrues gradually with sustained, useful contributions, while creating many identities yields only shallow roots and no real power.
